prompt:
Prevent AWS credential refresh and SigV4 signing from blocking the event loop in these asynchronous LiteLLM routes: Bedrock single-input embedding requests (including Titan, Nova and TwelveLabs), async invoke status polling, ApplyGuardrail content checks, invoke guardrail checks, and Bedrock Mantle requests. Credential loading and request preparation/signing on these paths must run in a worker thread so unrelated coroutines can make progress during a blocking refresh.

Preserve the existing sign_request_off_loop_if_aws interface and make it recognize Mantle configurations as AWS signers even though Mantle uses a composed signer. Do not require a particular new marker class or inheritance design. Preserve existing synchronous signing and the request methods, headers, payloads and returned response shapes. Signed requests must still contain the SigV4 Authorization header and use the supplied credentials. Bearer-token authentication must keep its existing behavior and avoid the SigV4 credential chain. Signing errors must propagate to the awaiting caller. Keep the changes scoped to these async signing and credential-loading paths; do not redesign AWS authentication.

prompt:
A post-call policy pipeline can deliver guardrail rewrites into buffered streaming responses. If the returned tool-call list has a different number of calls from the list given to the guardrail, discard that step's entire rewrite and deliver its original buffered chunks. Apply this to both dropped and added calls, even on translations that normally support writing back text and tool-call changes. Do not partially deliver associated text changes from the discarded step.

Cover Chat completion chunks, Anthropic SSE and Responses events through the existing streaming pipeline. Use the existing warning behavior: log at WARNING on the LiteLLM Proxy logger, naming the guardrail and including "discarded". Preserve the existing applied-guardrail/header behavior. Same-count tool-call edits and text rewrites continue to follow the translation's write-back capability, and non-writing translations retain their existing discard behavior. Preserve existing handling of absent tool-call fields. Do not redesign the non-streaming guardrail path.

prompt:
Run applicable post_call policy pipelines when a background Responses API result is retrieved. In the aget_responses request-processing path, attach the response's model-scoped policies after pre_call_hook has run, since that hook may decode or replace the response_id. Resolve the originating model group from the response ID's deployment identity through the existing router. Use that model group together with the current caller's team alias, key alias and request tags for policy matching, then attach only post_call pipelines. Preserve existing metadata conventions for pipeline definitions, pipeline-managed guardrails, applied policies/guardrails and policy sources. Avoid attaching a policy twice. Use the model group for matching without rewriting the retrieval's model field.

Do not perform this response-ID attachment on the aresponses submission path. Missing policy engine, router, resolvable response identity, model or applicable post_call policy must not produce a new failure. Preserve unrelated request metadata and already attached pipelines.

Defer policy-pipeline execution while a ResponsesAPIResponse is queued or in_progress. The post-call success hook must preserve the pending response, avoid invoking those pipeline guardrails, and log at DEBUG with the affected policy name and status. For completed or incomplete responses, run the post_call pipelines normally, including their blocking behavior. Remove the old pre-call warning that background requests with post_call pipelines are ungoverned. Preserve other callback and non-background behavior. No new helper name or module layout is required.

prompt:
Allow legacy post-call guardrails to run as policy-pipeline steps on buffered streams. A guardrail with its own async_post_call_success_hook must be eligible even without unified apply_guardrail support, including guardrails that opt into native lifecycle hooks. Invoke the legacy hook once with the standard data, user API key and assembled response in the endpoint's native non-streaming shape.

Add the translation interface BaseTranslation.post_call_hook_response(response), whose default returns its input unchanged. AnthropicMessagesHandler implements the same method: convert an assembled OpenAI ModelResponse into an Anthropic Messages response, preserving text, finish reason and input/output usage; for an ordinary completed text response this means type=message, role=assistant, text content blocks and stop_reason=end_turn. Non-ModelResponse inputs retain their identity.

If the legacy hook returns None, release the original stream. If it returns a replacement, rescan through the same endpoint translation. Deliver rewritten text only when it aligns one-to-one with the original scanned text and the translation supports ended-stream write-back. If the rewrite cannot be delivered, restore original chunks, let the step pass and warn with the guardrail name and "discarded". Preserve other stream events. A blocking exception must terminate delivery with that exception; other errors retain the pipeline's on_error semantics. A missing endpoint translation is an execution error.

A streaming pipeline is eligible only if every step supports unified execution or has its own legacy post-call success hook. An iterator-hook-only guardrail does not qualify; skip that pipeline with a warning naming it and its unsupported guardrails, allowing their ordinary handling. Deferred end-of-stream auditing must not run a pipeline-managed legacy hook a second time. Preserve non-streaming behavior and existing pipeline result/metadata contracts; no new private helper naming is required.
